title: Two different strengths
teaching_goal: See that two answers can both be good in different ways, and say what each one gives up.
question: A customer calls, angry that their order is three days late. What do you do?

rubric.label: A concrete next step and when it happens

sentences.text: First I'd let them explain fully, without interrupting, because they need to feel heard before anything else lands.
I'd say I'm sorry it's late and that I understand how frustrating it is when you've planned around a delivery.
Then I'd look up the order while they're on the line and tell them what I can see.
I'd promise to call back by the end of the day with a firm date.
I'd apologise once and go straight to the order.
If the courier shows a new date, I'd give it to them and send it by text so they have it in writing.
If there's no date, I'd offer a replacement sent by next-day delivery or a refund, and let them choose.
Either way they'd leave the call with a decision made, not a promise to call back.

explanation.summary: Both answers would help this customer, in different ways. A puts the customer's feelings first and is careful not to over-promise; B gets to a decision quickly and gives the customer a choice. Neither is the one right answer.

strengths.why: Lets the customer be heard and names the frustration specifically.
Looks it up on the call instead of passing it on.

gaps.why: The customer leaves without a date; a callback is a promise they have to wait on.

A.uncertain: Whether the callback happens on time decides how this answer lands; the answer can't show that.

strengths.why: Concrete options with timing, and the customer chooses.
A decision on the call, not a follow-up.

gaps.why: A single quick apology may feel rushed to someone who is angry.

B.uncertain: Whether the speaker can offer a replacement or refund depends on what the company allows; the answer assumes it.

explanation.alternatives: Many good answers mix the two: a little more acknowledgement than B, a firmer next step than A. Choosing either and saying why is a good answer to this exercise.

review_status: Written for practice with fictional details; checked for consistency, not reviewed by an outside interviewer.
